question: The following vehicles are all moving at a velocity of 50 km/hr. All the vehicles need to be stopped at the same point. Which vehicle has to apply more force in breaks to stop the vehicle?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Force required to stop a moving vehicle** is directly proportional to the vehicle's **mass** and its velocity. Since all vehicles are moving at the same velocity (50 km/hr), the determining factor here is the mass of the vehicle.
 
• A **bus** has significantly more mass compared to a bicycle, car, or scooter. Hence, it will require more force to bring it to a stop.
 
• The equation for force is derived from Newton's second law of motion:
 
 
• **F = ma**, where F is force, m is mass, and a is acceleration (or deceleration in this case).
 
• A larger mass (bus) will result in a greater force being required to achieve the same deceleration.
 
 
 
• The stopping distance and braking force also depend on the **kinetic energy** of the vehicle, which is given by the formula: **K.E. = 1/2 mv²**. Since the velocity (v) is constant for all vehicles, the kinetic energy is directly proportional to the mass. The bus, having the highest mass, possesses the highest kinetic energy and hence requires the most force to stop.
 
• **Frictional forces** between the tires and the road surface, as well as the efficiency of the braking system, also play a role. However, the primary determinant in this scenario remains the mass of the vehicle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:**

 
 
• This law states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration (F = ma).
 
• In the context of braking, negative acceleration (deceleration) is applied to bring the vehicle to a stop. A heavier vehicle like a bus requires more force to achieve the same deceleration as a lighter vehicle.
 
 
 
• **Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion and is given by the formula K.E. = 1/2 mv².
 
• As the mass of the vehicle increases, its kinetic energy increases proportionally, making it harder to stop the vehicle. This is why a bus, being the heaviest among the given options, requires the most force to stop.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Braking Force:**
 
 
• The mass of the vehicle: Heavier vehicles require more force to stop.
 
• The velocity of the vehicle: Higher speeds result in greater kinetic energy, requiring more force for deceleration.
 
• The condition of the brakes: Well-maintained brakes can generate higher frictional force, aiding in quicker stopping.
 
• Road conditions: Slippery or uneven surfaces can reduce the effectiveness of braking.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• In real-world scenarios, heavy vehicles like buses and trucks require longer stopping distances and more robust braking systems compared to lighter vehicles such as bicycles or scooters.
 
• Highway safety measures often account for the increased stopping distance of heavy vehicles by providing longer braking zones.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Braking Systems:** Advanced braking systems like Anti-lock Braking System (ABS) are used in modern vehicles to prevent skidding and reduce stopping distance, especially in heavy vehicles like buses.
 
• **Momentum:** The momentum of a vehicle is the product of its mass and velocity (p = mv). A bus has a greater momentum than a bicycle, car, or scooter at the same velocity, requiring more force to stop.
 
• **Energy Dissipation:** Brakes convert the kinetic energy of a moving vehicle into heat energy. A bus, with higher kinetic energy, generates more heat during braking, requiring a more efficient braking system.
 
• **Real-life Application:** The design of braking systems for heavy vehicles takes into account their higher mass and momentum. This is why buses and trucks are equipped with air brakes or hydraulic brakes, which provide greater stopping power.
